name: Pediatric lateral approach to the proximal femur
aliases: pediatric vastus lateralis approach to proximal femur
corridor: Lateral fascia-lata and vastus lateralis window aligned with the femoral-neck axis for screws or a pediatric hip locking plate

positioning.text: Position so the lateral proximal femur and femoral-neck axis can be imaged and the incision aligned with planned implants.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the greater trochanter and the femoral-neck axis so screws in the neck line up with that axis; prolong the mark distally when a plate is planned.

incision.text: Place the incision along the neck axis and extend it distally far enough for plate fixation, drill guides, and jigs when an angular-stable plate is used. Image intensification helps site the cut.

superficial_interval.text: Incise fascia lata in line with the skin incision.

deep_interval.text: Incise the vastus lateralis origin with a longitudinal or L-shaped cut and elevate the muscle from the femur.

layers.text: Skin, fascia lata, vastus lateralis, and the lateral femoral cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The medial femoral circumflex artery is the key vascular structure of the proximal femur and must be respected if dissection approaches the capsule; stay cranial to piriformis and keep obturator externus intact.

danger_zones.text: Capsule preparation, if performed, must remain cranial to piriformis where the medial femoral circumflex artery enters the joint.

retraction_hazards.text: Elevate vastus lateralis only as far as the implant requires; angular-stable plates need extra distal room for jigs.

exposure.text: Exposes the lateral proximal femur for screws or a pediatric hip locking plate, including when combined with a separate anterior reduction.

limitations.text: Used for implant insertion and for extracapsular or nondisplaced intracapsular fixation; displaced intracapsular work still needs a companion anterior approach.

indications.text: Indicated with an anterior approach for screw or pediatric hip-locking-plate insertion, for open or closed stabilization of extracapsular fractures, and for nondisplaced intracapsular fractures.

complications.text: Complications include avascular necrosis if proximal dissection injures the medial femoral circumflex artery.

procedure_applications.condition: Screws or a pediatric hip locking plate are inserted from the lateral femur, including after a separate anterior reduction

questions.question: How should the lateral incision be aligned?
questions.answer: So that screws in the femoral neck line up with the neck axis.

questions.question: When is this lateral window combined with an anterior approach?
questions.answer: When screws or a pediatric hip locking plate are inserted after anterior reduction.

questions.question: Why do angular-stable plates need a longer distal incision?
questions.answer: To accommodate drill guides and jigs.
